transcript: Yesterday I went to see Primary Trust off Broadway at roundabout, a new place during William Jackson Harper s Kenneth, a man whose past trauma and circumstances have in some ways pushed him to cling to a life astringent routine and solitude. This is disrupted when the bookstore he's worked out for almost 20 years is closing and he needs to find a new job. The production is smartly crafted. The set design is like a scale down model of Rochester suburb where it takes place, and a couple of the supporting actors play multiple characters that come and go fluidly throughout the piece. These choices reflect the quaint and monotonous lifestyle that Kenneth is living and the interchangeability of the people he encounters. This is a one act, 95 minute play that paints a really deep portrait of a man grappling with anxiety and loneliness and his efforts to move forward when a push comes. I was really impressed with this production, particularly in its vulnerability and its subtlety. I trust is running at the Laura Pals Theater until July second with that another playbill for my collection.
